scope: Topcoat 0.12.1 documentation and source, including explicitly enabled first-party features and named external integrations. The framework remains experimental; rendering benchmarks separately retain Topcoat 0.3.1.

ssr.note: Async Rust view components render markup on the server.

streaming.note: live!() and emit!() send initial HTML and later region updates over the original HTTP response. Available since 0.7; verified in 0.12.1. Optional WebSocket updates can continue after the initial page load.

suspense.note: The built-in suspense component shows fallback UI while async child content loads, then streams the result into place. Available since 0.7; verified in 0.12.1.

client.note: Reactive Rust expressions compile to JavaScript that activates server-rendered UI; shards can replace server-rendered fragments.
client.label: Compiled JS

ssg.note: Static export and prerendering remain unchecked roadmap items in Topcoat 0.12.1.
ssg.label: Roadmap

csr.note: Compiled reactive expressions update server-authored UI. A standalone CSR application root is not established.
csr.label: Server-authored runtime

serverOnly.note: Rust view/component code renders on the server; explicitly reactive expressions compile to JavaScript.

partialRendering.note: The 0.12.1 README still lists static export and prerendering as roadmap work. live!/emit! stream runtime updates; that does not establish a retained prerendered shell with request-time holes.

routing.note: Pages, layouts, and API routes support manual or auto-discovered routers.

layouts.note: Module layouts wrap routed pages and compose app-level structure.

dynamicRoutes.note: Page/API route macros support typed path and query parameters.

parallelRoutes.note: The reviewed module router does not establish independently navigable named slots.

interceptedRoutes.note: The reviewed router does not define intercepted-modal and direct-entry rendering semantics.

prefetch.note: Runtime links prefetch on intent by default, with viewport and never modes configurable per link/context. Prefetch is best effort and may be skipped for data-saving or concurrent-load policy; plain anchors keep normal navigation.
prefetch.label: Runtime link prefetch

softNavigation.note: runtime::link and link_attrs navigate server-rendered pages without a full reload. Shared signals can survive reconciliation; external targets, downloads and incompatible responses use normal document navigation.
softNavigation.label: Runtime links

viewTransitions.note: The reviewed routing API does not establish this navigation capability. Application code or another package may provide it; this finding is not proof of absence.

redirects.note: Router errors/helpers support temporary and permanent redirects, 303 POST/Redirect/GET and internal rewrite redispatch. These are HTTP/router APIs; proxy deployment still requires explicit mount/origin configuration.
redirects.label: Redirect / rewrite helpers

serverData.note: Async view functions load data directly and share request/app context.

clientData.note: Procedures/shards can request server results and replace UI. A browser query cache with retry/stale-data policy is not established.
clientData.label: Procedures / shards

requestDedupe.note: #[memoize] shares a request-context function result by arguments within one request.

persistentCache.note: Request memoization is documented; an across-request data/page cache is not established.

invalidation.note: The reviewed memoization lifecycle ends with the request; cross-request dependency/tag invalidation is not established.

isr.note: The reviewed route API does not establish retained static-page regeneration.

apiRoutes.note: Route macros register HTTP API handlers alongside pages.

httpErrors.note: Topcoat 0.12.1 maps router errors to their HTTP status and other unhandled errors to 500. A fallback view can explicitly select StatusCode::NOT_FOUND. Error-boundary documentation states that handlers can change status only before the response starts streaming; a late fallback cannot retroactively change it.
httpErrors.label: Router errors / status in views

actions.note: Procedures are documented as async server functions callable from the browser.
actions.label: Procedures

forms.note: Route Form<T> extraction deserializes native query/form submissions into typed values, and documented examples use POST/Redirect/GET. Parsing failures map to HTTP errors; business validation and field-error feedback remain application-owned. A general validation framework is still roadmap work.
forms.label: Typed native form submissions

middleware.note: Router layers wrap request handling with body, context and Next, and can apply across route prefixes. Optional TowerLayer/TowerRoute bridge external middleware/services. A helper function alone is not the complete middleware API.
middleware.label: Router layers

cookies.note: Cookie helpers support signed/encrypted and prefixed cookies; sessions accept app-supplied storage.

cssModules.note: The reviewed view/style APIs do not document CSS Modules class-map compilation.

scopedCss.note: Views accept authored classes/styles; component-local selector rewriting is not established.

tailwind.note: The optional Tailwind integration runs the external compiler and bundles generated CSS.

cssInJs.note: Compiled reactive style expressions do not establish a CSS-in-JS compiler/SSR registry.

images.note: Image optimization/resizing remains an unchecked roadmap item in 0.12.1; asset hashing and downloading do not transform images.
images.label: Roadmap

fonts.note: Font utilities download/bundle Fontsource fonts as application assets; this does not imply every font has automatic subsetting.

scripts.note: Topcoat manages generated client expressions; arbitrary third-party script scheduling is application-owned.
scripts.label: Compiled client runtime

assetPipeline.note: Topcoat 0.12.1’s asset! macro produces a typed asset URL. The asset bundler hashes file contents, emits fingerprinted filenames and a manifest, and the router serves the matching bundle. Deploy the binary and asset bundle from the same build. Assets outside this pipeline remain application-owned.
assetPipeline.label: asset! / asset bundle

staticAssets.note: asset! discovers, copies/downloads, and fingerprints application assets.

metadata.note: The built-in Metadata API supplies structured title, description, canonical, robots, Open Graph and X fields; metadata::tags renders the combined document head. The feature is enabled by default.
metadata.label: Structured Metadata API

dynamicMetadata.note: Metadata::from_fn loads request-dependent metadata asynchronously through Cx before the outer layout renders. Request memoization can share data with the page body.
dynamicMetadata.label: Async Metadata::from_fn

metadataInheritance.note: Router defaults, outer-to-inner layouts and page metadata combine field by field. Unset fields inherit; request child contexts can override the combined values. An Open Graph image list is replaced as one field.
metadataInheritance.label: Field-level inheritance

metadataOverrides.note: Page/inner metadata replaces fields independently, and no_* removal methods block inheritance for selected fields. Open Graph image lists replace as a whole rather than merging every item.
metadataOverrides.label: Overrides / explicit removals

titleTemplates.note: Title text can be rendered by application views; an ancestor title-template API is not established.

socialImages.note: Asset downloads/fingerprints do not establish dynamic social-card image generation.

sitemaps.note: The optional sitemap feature supplies Sitemap and SitemapUrl response types with last-modified, frequency and priority. Relative URLs resolve with BaseUrl; application code chooses/enumerates entries.
sitemaps.label: Sitemap response types

robots.note: With the fs feature, public_dir serves an application public directory at the site root, allowing an authored robots.txt to retain its required public URL. A fingerprinted asset! URL alone is not the robots.txt convention; directive contents remain application-owned.
robots.label: Unchanged public file

markdown.note: Markdown support remains a roadmap item in 0.12.1; rendering authored HTML or an email plain-text alternative is a different feature.
markdown.label: Markdown support planned

collections.note: Assets are bundled; typed content collection schemas/loaders/query APIs are not established.

draftMode.note: Request functions can authorize a preview; a dedicated draft/cache-bypass mode is not established.

translations.note: The optional first-party l10n/Fluent features load message catalogs, interpolate arguments and apply locale fallback. topcoat l10n check validates message keys/variables; applications choose supported locales.
translations.label: Fluent catalogs / l10n

localeRouting.note: Locale implements route parameter parsing, and the localization guide composes a locale segment with request layers and Accept-Language negotiation. The application chooses supported locales and redirect/fallback policy.
localeRouting.label: Locale parameters / negotiation

localeFormatting.note: The l10n-number and l10n-datetime features format numbers and dates for the request locale. Documented limitations include no currency/percent formatting and limited date/time styles; enable the relevant features.
localeFormatting.label: Optional locale formatters

auth.note: Authentication remains a roadmap item in 0.12.1. Cookie/session primitives require application-owned account lookup, credential verification and identity storage.
auth.label: Roadmap

csp.note: The reviewed generated-JavaScript runtime does not document coordinated CSP nonce/hash policy.

cspNonce.note: The reviewed security/rendering API does not establish coordinated per-response CSP nonces for generated scripts and styles. Hash-based CSP and application-authored headers are different mechanisms.

csrf.note: OriginPolicy rejects cross-origin browser mutations and cross-origin WebSocket handshakes before request layers by default. Trusted origins or explicit disabling are configurable. This is origin enforcement, not a token service or authentication.
csrf.label: Default OriginPolicy

environment.note: Server context can hold configuration; explicitly compiled client expressions must not expose secrets. A public/private environment namespace is not established.
environment.label: Request / app context

types.note: Rust checks server components and the typed expressions accepted by the reactive compiler.

hmr.note: Development hooks notify the dev server about rebuild/readiness and display status; this does not establish state-preserving hot replacement.
hmr.label: Dev rebuild integration

cli.note: Existing tooling bundles assets; project scaffolding via topcoat new is still on the roadmap.
cli.label: Asset tooling

bundleAnalysis.note: Asset discovery/bundling is documented; a production module-size analysis view is not established.

unitTests.note: Views/helpers use Rust tests with a fresh Cx::new() populated through Cx::with. This supplies context construction, not a browser test runner; application tests must arrange their own dependencies.
unitTests.label: Rust tests / explicit context

e2eTests.note: The reviewed runtime docs do not provide a browser end-to-end test integration.

observability.note: Request context exposes headers/extensions; a maintained tracing/metrics integration is not established.

errorHandling.note: The built-in error_boundary component catches child view failures and renders a supplied fallback; returning Err propagates upward. A fallback must explicitly choose an HTTP error status before streaming begins.
errorHandling.label: View error_boundary

serverHosting.note: serve/serve_until run a router from a TCP listener with graceful shutdown.

subpathProxy.note: Topcoat 0.12.1 provides a public BaseUrl with an optional path prefix and helpers for absolute URLs; assets can use a separately configured external base. These helpers do not establish automatic rebasing of every route, relative link and live request. The proxy mount and application URL use must be coordinated explicitly.
subpathProxy.label: BaseUrl; proxy-owned mount

staticHosting.note: A complete static export remains an unchecked roadmap item in 0.12.1; publishing bundled assets alone is not an exported application.
staticHosting.label: Roadmap

containers.note: Deployment documentation is an unchecked roadmap item; a maintained container recipe is not established.

edgeHosting.note: A published 0.12.1 example runs Router::handle from a Cloudflare Worker fetch handler without the native serve feature. It buffers request bodies and does not support runtime WebSocket connections on Workers.
edgeHosting.label: Cloudflare Worker example

orm.note: The recommended scaffold and todo example integrate the first-party Toasty ORM with SQLite. Enable/install that integration; Topcoat’s renderer does not itself supply the database or query engine.
orm.label: Toasty integration

migrations.note: The recommended Toasty scaffold documents generating and applying versioned migrations through the application CLI. Migration execution/history belongs to Toasty rather than the view renderer.
migrations.label: Toasty migrations

transactions.note: The reviewed framework documentation does not establish an owned transactions API. Host libraries and application integrations may provide it.

jobs.note: A durable background-job system remains roadmap work in 0.12.1.
jobs.label: Background jobs planned

mail.note: The optional mail feature provides typed mail builders, HTML/plain-text bodies, attachments and transport APIs. SMTP needs mail-smtp and transport configuration; acceptance by a transport is not inbox delivery or a durable job queue.
mail.label: Mail builders / transports

uploads.note: The optional multipart extractor streams form fields/files and enforces configured body limits. Durable storage, file validation and cloud-object lifecycle remain application/library work.
uploads.label: Multipart transport

realtime.note: Optional WebSocket and SSE response types provide real-time transports, and connected live views can continue over a runtime WebSocket. Applications still own authentication, fan-out/storage and distributed pub/sub.
realtime.label: Live views / WebSocket / SSE

xssEscaping.note: view! escapes interpolated values. Explicit raw/unescaped APIs require trusted content and do not sanitize rich HTML; compiled browser-expression captures must still exclude secrets.
xssEscaping.label: Escaped view interpolation

htmlSanitization.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific html sanitization contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

authorization.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific authorization policies contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

rateLimiting.note: The roadmap still lists easier-to-use middleware such as rate limiting. Runtime WebSocket render limits are a narrower resource cap, not a general request-rate limiter.
rateLimiting.label: Rate-limiting middleware planned

progressiveEnhancement.note: The Toasty todo example submits ordinary HTML forms to server handlers, mutates the database and redirects. That submission path works without the client runtime; reactive procedures/shards are separate enhancements.
progressiveEnhancement.label: Native POST / redirect forms

optimisticUi.note: The linked data API review does not establish the specific optimistic updates contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

requestCancellation.note: When shard arguments change, a new request aborts the earlier pending request so the latest arguments win. This is client request/stale-result handling; a server mutation may already have taken effect.
requestCancellation.label: Latest shard request wins

typedLinks.note: href!(handler, named_parameter: value) constructs route-aware links with generated parameter bindings, encoding and compile-time checking of required arguments. The API also accepts raw paths, which do not gain equivalent route-name guarantees.
typedLinks.label: Typed href! helpers

searchParams.note: query_params derives a typed deserializer and caches the parsed request query. Malformed inputs return a QueryParamsError or a configured HTTP error/redirect. This is server request state, not a browser query-state synchronization library.
searchParams.label: Typed query_params

stateRestoration.note: Runtime navigation preserves signals shared by both pages, and shard updates retain matching signal/input state. Preservation depends on identity; this is not durable restoration after reload or a guarantee that every departed page remains mounted.
stateRestoration.label: Shared-signal retention

scrollRestoration.note: Runtime navigation scrolls new pages to the top or fragment and restores saved scroll on back/forward. The documented behavior covers page navigation, not arbitrary independently scrolling containers.
scrollRestoration.label: Runtime history scroll

navigationBlocking.note: The linked routing API review does not establish the specific unsaved-change guards contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

navigationAccessibility.note: The linked client rendering API review does not establish the specific accessible navigation contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

a11yChecks.note: The linked client rendering API review does not establish the specific accessibility checks contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

lazyActivation.note: Islands remain a roadmap item; reactive expressions and streaming alone do not establish configurable idle/visible/interaction activation.
lazyActivation.label: Islands planned

codeSplitting.note: The linked rendering API review does not establish the specific route / island splitting contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

offline.note: The linked deployment API review does not establish the specific offline integration contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

scheduling.note: The linked backend API review does not establish the specific scheduled tasks contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

notifications.note: The linked backend API review does not establish the specific multi-channel notifications contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

searchIndex.note: The linked backend API review does not establish the specific search indexing contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

fieldEncryption.note: The linked database API review does not establish the specific encrypted model fields contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

httpTests.note: The linked testing API review does not establish the specific http integration tests contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.
